text:
Maya Patel: Heads up — I posted a draft of the audit event taxonomy in the shared drive. Need a quick cross-team check: naming conventions, what fields are customer-visible, and how KMS/key ids should appear in events. Can folks skim and call out major red flags?
Jordan Lee: on it. quick q — are we keeping the top-level namespace `audit.` or do we prefer `event.audit.`?
Maya Patel: leaning toward `audit.` to keep emitted names short. main principle: dotted, lower-case, verb-first action naming (e.g. `audit.user.create`).
Li Chen: agree with dotted lowercase. Also: we should separate `action` vs `outcome` in the schema — action like `user.create` and outcome `success|failure|denied`. Keeps event names focused.
Sasha Rodriguez: +1. also need to define which events are customer-facing (in org's audit exports) vs internal-only (debug/infra). Customers must never see long-lived secrets or raw KMS ciphertexts.
Maya Patel: yep. thinking three visibility tiers: `customer`, `internal`, `sensitive`. We'll add `visibility` enum to the schema.
Jordan Lee: can we standardize required fields? I propose: `event_name`, `timestamp`, `request_id`, `actor:{id,type,role}`, `resource:{type,id}`, `action`, `outcome`, `visibility`. Optional: `kms_key_id` only when key-related ops occur.
Li Chen: thanks. For KMS, we need `kms_key_id` as an opaque id, never the key material. For BYOK flows we might need `key_owner_org` for auditability, but mark as `sensitive` visibility.
Sasha Rodriguez: RBAC angle — when role escalation happens we should log `actor.previous_role` and `actor.new_role` and mark outcome if a policy denied or allowed. Also include `policy_id` if applicable.
Maya Patel: good catch. Add `actor.previous_role` and `actor.new_role` optional fields.
AuditBot: automated check: submitted sample event failed schema lint: `event_name` contains uppercase and spaces. Rule: `^[a-z0-9]+(\.[a-z0-9]+)*$`. Please reformat.
Jordan Lee: oops, my sample had `Audit.User Create`. Will fix.
Maya Patel: sample naming we should propose in the RFC. Draft snippet:```
# recommended event names
audit.user.create
audit.user.delete
audit.session.start
audit.kms.key.rotate
audit.kms.key.create
audit.rbac.role.assign
```
Li Chen: those look clean. For customer exports we should map internal infra events to friendlier names or filter them out — customers only need `audit.user.*`, `audit.session.*`, `audit.kms.key.*` (key lifecycle), and `audit.rbac.*` for role changes.
Sasha Rodriguez: Is there an explicit list of PII fields that must be redacted before export? e.g., `actor.email`, `resource.path` might contain emails.
Maya Patel: Yes — add `redaction_rules` to the export pipeline. We'll publish a small table: field -> redaction strategy (hash, truncate, omit).
Jordan Lee: cross-team compatibility: eng-platform/analytics will want `event_name` tokens to be stable for at least 12 months. Any rename must go through a migration alias.
Maya Patel: agree. We'll require `deprecated_names` array in the schema metadata (not in each event) and plan a deprecation cycle.
Li Chen: about RBAC changes: when we change role semantics, we must link the audit event to the effective policy version: `policy_version` field. That helps incident triage.
Sasha Rodriguez: vuln triage note — if an audit export shows repeated `audit.kms.key.create` for the same key id from unknown actor, we should auto-create a P1 alert. We should define heuristics in the playbook.
Maya Patel: action items: 1) finalize naming regex and publish naming examples (I'll update the draft) 2) add `visibility` enum + default mapping for export flows (Jordan to coordinate) 3) KMS fields: `kms_key_id` opaque, `key_owner_org` marked sensitive (Li to draft) 4) RBAC role-change fields + `policy_version` (Sasha to draft playbook) 5) add lint rule in AuditBot for event_name and required fields (eng-platform)
Jordan Lee: I'll add the AuditBot rule. Example check pseudocode:```
if not regex_match(event.event_name, "^[a-z0-9]+(\\.[a-z0-9]+)*$"):
    reject("invalid event_name")
required = ["event_name","timestamp","request_id","actor.id","action","outcome","visibility"]
for r in required:
    if not has_field(event, r): reject("missing " + r)
```
AuditBot: note: added lint rule to staging; will start rejecting events that fail `event_name` format next week.
Maya Patel: Great. One more UX question — customers expect human-readable labels in the audit UI. We'll keep `event_name` as the canonical key and add `display_name` optional for UI (not for programmatic matching).
Li Chen: sounds good. Also recommend including `service` field (e.g., `redwood.inference.runtime`) to help multi-service pipelines.
Sasha Rodriguez: final: encryption telemetry — do we include `encryption.applied: true/false`? Might be helpful to spot unlabeled plaintext logs.
Maya Patel: ok add `encryption.applied` boolean to events that touch data and `kms_key_id` if true. Mark `encryption.*` fields sensitive for exports.
Jordan Lee: I'll assemble a short RFC and a compatibility checklist for eng teams — include migration aliases and AuditBot lint rollout plan.
Maya Patel: thanks everyone. I'll update the draft and ping product + legal for customer-facing wording. Meeting if needed next Tue 10am.
Sasha Rodriguez: :thumbsup:
AuditBot: reminder scheduled: RFC review deadline in 5 days.
